# Nutrition Plan for Powerlifting

## Calorie Target
**2,800-3,200 calories/day** (slight surplus to build muscle)
- BMR ~1,800 + activity burn + surplus

## Macronutrient Breakdown

| Macro | Daily Target | Purpose |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| **Protein** | 170-200g | Muscle repair & growth |
| **Carbs** | 350-450g | Training energy & recovery |
| **Fats** | 80-100g | Hormone production |

## Priority Foods

**Proteins** (170-200g)
- Chicken, beef, fish
- Eggs, Greek yogurt
- Cottage cheese, whey protein

**Carbs** (350-450g)
- Rice, oats, potatoes
- Pasta, bread
- Fruits & vegetables

**Fats** (80-100g)
- Olive oil, nuts
- Avocados, fatty fish
- Whole eggs

## Key Principles
- ✅ Eat 0.8-1g protein per pound of body weight
- ✅ Time carbs around training (pre/post-workout)
- ✅ Stay hydrated (3-4L water daily)
- ✅ Track intake for 2-3 weeks to dial in amounts
- ✅ Adjust calories if not gaining ~0.5-1 lb/week

**Consider:** Work with a sports nutritionist for a personalized plan tied to your training cycle.

# Nutrition Plan for Marathon Training

## Daily Calorie Target
**~2,800-3,200 calories** (depending on run intensity and cross-training)

## Macronutrient Breakdown

| Macro | Daily Target | Purpose |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| **Carbs** | 55-60% (385-480g) | Fuel for long runs & glycogen replenishment |
| **Protein** | 15-20% (105-160g) | Muscle recovery & adaptation |
| **Fat** | 20-25% (60-90g) | Hormonal health & satiety |

---

## Meal Timing Around 2-Hour Morning Run

### **Pre-Run (45-60 min before)**
- Easy-to-digest carbs + minimal fiber/fat
- Examples: banana + honey, toast with jam, sports drink, oatmeal

### **During Run (if >90 min)**
- 30-60g carbs/hour
- Sports drink, gels, or energy chews

### **Post-Run (within 30-60 min) — CRITICAL**
- **3:1 carb:protein ratio** (e.g., 60g carbs + 20g protein)
- Examples: chocolate milk, bagel + Greek yogurt, rice + chicken, smoothie with fruit & protein powder

---

## Sample Daily Menu

| Meal | Examples |
|------|----------|
| **Breakfast (post-run)** | Oatmeal (60g) + banana + egg whites, OR bagel + peanut butter + berries |
| **Mid-Morning Snack** | Greek yogurt + granola, or sports bar |
| **Lunch** | Chicken/fish + brown rice + vegetables + olive oil |
| **Afternoon Snack** | Fruit + nuts, or smoothie |
| **Dinner** | Lean protein + pasta/potatoes + veggies |
| **Hydration** | 3-4L water daily; electrolytes on long run days |

---

## Key Principles
✅ **Prioritize carbs strategically** around training  
✅ **Hydrate consistently** throughout the day  
✅ **Eat protein at every meal** for recovery  
✅ **Include whole grains, lean proteins, fruits, vegetables**  
✅ **Experiment during training** before race day

Would you like specific meal prep ideas or adjustments?

# Competition Day Meal Plan (2400 kcal)

## Pre-Competition Strategy
**Timing matters more than usual today.** Space meals 2-3 hours apart to avoid GI distress during matches.

---

## BREAKFAST (6-7 AM) — 600 kcal
- **2 cups white rice** (cooked) — 260 kcal
- **3 tbsp peanut butter** — 280 kcal
- **1 banana** (peeled, easier to digest) — 60 kcal

*Why: Quick carbs + fat for sustained energy, minimal fiber*

---

## MID-MORNING SNACK (9 AM) — 400 kcal
- **White bread sandwich** (2 slices):
  - 2 tbsp peanut butter — 190 kcal
  - 1 tbsp honey — 60 kcal
- **Sports drink** (500ml, 6-8% carbs) — 150 kcal

*Why: Easily digestible carbs, keeps blood sugar stable*

---

## LUNCH (11:30 AM) — 700 kcal
- **White basmati rice** (1.5 cups cooked) — 195 kcal
- **Tofu stir-fry** (200g firm tofu, cooked in oil) — 280 kcal
- **White noodles or rice vermicelli** (75g dry) — 225 kcal

*Why: Complete protein, low-fiber carbs, easily digestible*

---

## PRE-MATCH SNACK (30-45 min before first match) — 300 kcal
- **Refined white bread** (2 slices) — 140 kcal
- **2 tbsp honey or jam** — 110 kcal
- **Water or electrolyte drink** — 50 kcal

*Why: Quick glucose, won't sit heavy in stomach*

---

## POST-MATCH (If multiple matches) — 400 kcal
- **Sports drink** (750ml) — 250 kcal
- **White rice cakes + peanut butter** — 150 kcal

*Why: Rapid carb/electrolyte replenishment*

---

## KEY PRINCIPLES
✓ **Refined carbs only** (white rice, white bread, pasta)  
✓ **No whole grains, beans, or high-fiber vegetables**  
✓ **Adequate protein** (tofu, peanut butter, nuts)  
✓ **Hydration**: Sip water/electrolytes throughout  
✓ **Smaller, frequent portions** to avoid bloating  
✗ Avoid: Dairy, seeds, raw vegetables, anything greasy 2+ hours before weigh-in

**Weigh-in specifics?** If you cut weight yesterday, this maintains today without adding water retention.
